title: Handoff note
description: The YAML in the `aidd-handoff` block a role ends each run with (references/handoff.md). It is a report from an agent, so it is data: never a person's yes, and never evidence. `aidd validate` warns about a note that breaks this shape, and about hidden characters or text posing as a person's words in it. It advises and blocks nothing. The latest note in a document counts. `next` is checked against the roles in roles.json, `status` against the Spec statuses, and the first word of `stopped_at` against the stop codes, because those lists have their own owners.

done.description: What the run did, with the evidence it names. Debt found and left goes here as `debt: <what, where>`.

next_role.description: The role that takes the work next, such as `verifier`. A role, never an approval and never a person's decision.

needs.description: A decision only a person can give, in one sentence, or `none`. A choice between options points to a decision card.

stopped_at.description: Why the run stopped: one stop code (`stop_code` in the common schema), alone or followed by `: ` and any detail, such as `stopped_at: "ask: spec.approve SPEC-3"`, quoted because of the colon. `none` when nothing stopped it. In a headless run, `ask`, with the ask it reached.

by.description: Who wrote the note: an agent writes `agent:<harness id>/<model>`, the value of its commits' `Assisted-by`, such as `agent:claude-code/claude-opus-5-5`. `aidd eval work` counts the note's step under it, and without it under the commit that posted the note. It is a label the writer gave, never proof, and it decides nothing.

spend.description: The harness's count of the run's tokens or cost, copied, or `unknown`; never an estimate. A run seldom sees its own count, so it writes `unknown`, and the lead's journal holds the harness's count.

status.description: The Spec status the run stopped in (`aidd status` shows it): one of the Spec statuses.

head.description: The commit the run checked, such as the verifier's or the reviewer's head. A delegated merge needs the latest note to name its exact head with `needs: none`.

asked.description: What a person asked the role directly, and what the role did with it.

decided.description: What the role settled itself, each with what settled it.

open_decisions.description: Each risk or choice the role found and left for the lead to settle, as a role writes a risk it would otherwise keep as a note. The lead answers each before it merges the role's work, on the standards, the project's rules, and aidd's default: on a later note's `answered`, by the entry's `id` and one of its own `options[].choice`. A choice only a person can make goes on the lead's `needs`, naming the `id`, and a note with none leaves this out. It is data, never a person's yes. Under a delegation, Spec approval and a merge defer while an entry stands that no later note answers that way; `decided` text answers no entry. It differs from `needs`, which stops the run for a person, and from `decided`, which the role settled itself.

answered.description: The lead's answer to each `open_decisions` entry of an earlier note: the entry's `id` and the choice taken, which must be one of that entry's own `options[].choice`, written exactly. An entry is answered only this way, by a note after the one that holds it. It records which offered choice was taken, never that the choice was good. It is data, never a person's yes.

run.description: The run at this stop. Any role lists in `opened` what the run opened and whether it closed it. The lead's snapshot of a long run also holds the run's `id`, what it counted and spent, and when it can go on, so another session, machine, or person goes on from the note and a limit never restarts at zero. A block with no `id` holds only `opened`. It is data, never evidence and never a yes. A count left out is zero.

id.description: The run, in the record id format: the UTC time to the millisecond, then 8 hex characters.

attempt_counts.description: How many times each step started on a work item, by `<work item id>:<step code>`, such as `SPEC-3:spec.in_progress`.

send_back_counts.description: How many times Verify or Review sent each work item back to Implement, by work item id.

spend.description: The sum of the spend the run knows, as the harness counted it, such as `412000 tokens`, or `unknown`; never an estimate. Like the note's own `spend`, which is one step's.

unknown_spend_steps.description: How many steps of the run have no known spend, so a reader knows `spend` is a floor.

hours.description: The hours the run has used.

resumes_at.description: The earliest time the run can go on, UTC, such as `2026-11-12T10:00:00Z`: the time a `waiting` stop is waiting for. Left out when nothing waits on a clock. `aidd validate` warns when the latest note still waits after that day.

opened.description: Each thing the run opened that outlives a command, as schemas/lifecycles.json lists them: a role, a worktree, a branch, a background process, a port, a scratch folder, or a PR/MR. Each says whether the run closed it. One left open says why, and who closes it now, so its ownership passes by this note. The lead closes what a role leaves for it, and lists at the end of a change what is still open.

what.description: The thing, so a reader can find it: what it is and its path, port, or process id, such as `a page server on port 8000, process 4242`.

closed.description: Whether the run closed it before it wrote this note.

why.description: Why it stays open, such as `a person has not looked at the preview yet`. Required when `closed` is false.

closed_by.description: Who closes it now: the lead, or only a person, such as for a branch whose delete asks. Required when `closed` is false.

open_decision.description: One risk or choice a role leaves for the lead, with the ways to settle it. `aidd status` shows each one that no later note answers.

id.description: A short, stable key for the entry, unique among the note's entries, such as `no-tests-check`. A later note's `answered` names it.

what.description: The risk or the choice, in one sentence, such as a check that may now fail honest work.

choice.description: One way to settle it. A later note's `answered` names it exactly, so each choice of an entry differs from the others.

blocks.description: The honest work this choice would stop or slow, or `nothing`.

options.description: The ways to settle it, each with what it blocks.

answer.description: One answer to an earlier note's `open_decisions` entry.

id.description: The `id` of the entry it answers.

choice.description: The choice taken: one of that entry's `options[].choice`, written exactly.
